summary: Sustained 5xx elevation during large upload: upstream handoff latency + ephemeral routing reorder
description:
Issue summary: LexaHealth observed a rapid elevation in 5xx responses across their dedicated eu-west capacity during a large multipart upload + mixed chat/embedding workload. Errors appear as 502/504 from API Gateway and intermittent 5xx from upstream runtimes.

Impact: Multiple production endpoints returning ~8-18% 5xx rate for a 45-minute window. Customer reports degraded UX for in-flight uploads and streaming chat sessions. This is a paying Dedicated customer with high SLAs.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-13 03:07 UTC: sustained upload begins from customer automation ingest (large batching of multipart embedding uploads + chat bursts).
- 03:10 UTC: api-gateway 502/504s spike; latency increases.
- 03:12-03:35 UTC: error rate peaks, internal dashboards show routing queue length and accept-queue growth on specific apigw hosts.
- 03:40 UTC: initial mitigation (rate limiting ingress for that tenant) reduced error rate but not fully resolved.

Observed symptoms: 
- API Gateway logs show repeated "502 Upstream handoff timeout" and occasional "504 keepalive read timeout".
- Serving runtime logs show short-lived runtime restarts correlating with kube hotplug events (GPU hotplug / container reattach) at the same time as heavy prefetch invalidations.
- Prefetch/KV cache invalidation counts spike; kvcache lock waiters increase.
- Route planner shows fanout reorder events where requests were redirected between ephemeral runtime nodes instead of queued at stable backends.

Why this is unique/different from other 5xx patterns: The signal combines a) large multipart upload pressure, b) ephemeral runtime hotplug sequence (hotplugging GPUs into the node pool), and c) a routing handoff path that attempts immediate fanout to new ephemeral nodes rather than queuing or applying admission-control backpressure. The immediate fanout combined with kvcache invalidations caused upstream runtimes to become transiently overloaded and drop connections rather than serving requests, amplifying 5xxs across the customer's shard.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated tenant on eu-west with model redwood-open-7b pinned
2) Begin large multipart embedding uploads concurrently with several streaming chat sessions (simulate LexaHealth ingestion: 4 parallel upload clients + 12 concurrent streaming chat clients),
3) Trigger a simulated ephemeral node hotplug (scale-out + immediate attach of new GPU-backed runtimes) while prefetch is enabled and kvcache TTL is low
4) Observe API Gateway 502/504s and upstream runtime restarts in a monitoring window ~2-10 minutes after start
logs: apigw-eu-west-03: 2026-03-13T03:11:02Z ERROR http2: 502 Upstream handoff timeout tenant=lexahealth request_id=01A2B3C
runtime-eu-west-07: 2026-03-13T03:11:05Z WARN prefetch: kvcache invalidation burst=1.2k locks_waiting=54 shard=embed-12
runtime-eu-west-09: 2026-03-13T03:11:06Z ERROR runtime: received SIGTERM during attach; graceful shutdown elapsed=2s reason=gpu-hotplug-attach
apigw-eu-west-03: 2026-03-13T03:12:30Z WARN accept-queue: depth=28758 host=apigw-eu-west-03 tenant=lexahealth
investigation_notes: Initial alert from SRE flagged apigw accept-queue growth and high 502 rate for tenant shard.
Correlated runtime attach/hotplug events from the cluster autoscaler logs within the same 120s window as start of 5xx spike.
Observed kvcache invalidation rate and a backlog of prefetch ops; kvcache compaction was running concurrently on the same nodes.

Hypothesis A: Routing attempted immediate fanout to newly attached runtimes which had cold KV caches and were still initializing kernel selection; heavy prefetch + invalidation created CPU/io pressure and triggered watchdog restarts.
Hypothesis B: Admission control did not apply granular per-tenant shed when accept-queue exceeded threshold because hotplug events altered host health signals, causing misrouted requests.

Checked linked metrics: per-tenant request concurrency jumped to 600 concurrent inflight sockets; apigw worker threads saturated and returned upstream handoff errors rather than queueing to stable backends.
Cross-referenced Slack thread #support-lexahealth and channel #incidents-eu where customers posted stacktraces and we confirmed tenant-specific traffic pattern.
actions_taken: 03:18 UTC - Support applied emergency tenant-level ingress rate limit to LexaHealth to cap concurrency and reduce immediate 5xx impact.
03:25 UTC - SRE disabled aggressive prefetch for affected shard as a temporary measure to reduce kvcache invalidation pressure.
03:40 UTC - Routing team rolled out a quick server-side tweak to delay fanout to newly attached runtimes by 250ms during attach window (canary on 2 hosts) to test hypothesis.
03:55 UTC - Observed partial reduction in 5xx after rate limiting + prefetch disable; full recovery pending routing change validation.
We collected full logs and heap/disk metrics and attached to this ticket for postmortem.
next_steps: 1) Routing: implement and promote controlled fanout policy (hold new-node fanout until kvcache warm or use admission throttle) — owner: Alex P — high priority.
2) Runtime: add guard to defer SIGTERM during attach until in-flight prefetches drain or mark node as not-ready in route planner during attach — owner: Priya S.
3) SRE: run a replay load test in staging that reproduces large-multipart upload + streaming mix with simulated node hotplug to validate fix — owner: SRE team.
4) Follow-up postmortem to update runbooks and add a metric-driven automated tenant-level admission control for sustained accept-queue growth — owner: Support/Eng.
5) Notify LexaHealth with timeline and mitigation plan; schedule a joint verification window once a fix is staged.
Estimated ETA for codefix canary: 48-72 hours; full rollout pending test results.
resolution_summary: (In Progress) Temporary mitigations (tenant ingress-rate cap, disabling aggressive prefetch) reduced immediate 5xx rate. Engineering is preparing routing & runtime fixes to prevent immediate fanout to hotplugged nodes and to make attach events safer for heavy prefetch workloads. Final resolution pending code rollout and verification.

If customer asks: root cause appears to be a combination of routing fanout to newly-attached runtimes + heavy prefetch invalidations causing upstream overload and watch-dog restarts.
